newsitem.title: UK: Coffee vulnerable if funds liquidate, ICO says.
newsitem.headline: Coffee vulnerable if funds liquidate, ICO says.

text.p: The International Coffee Organization (ICO) said on Monday that spiralling coffee markets face a risk of big falls in prices if investment funds liquidate their massive positions built over the past few months.

In the meantime, the sharp price rally since January this year could be sustained ahead of the approaching Brazilian frost season in June and July, the ICO said in a document tabled at an executive board meeting and seen by Reuters.

The London-based ICO administers a producer-consumer coffee agreement. Its week-long meetings run parallel with those pf the sellers' Association of Coffee Producing Countries, led by Brazil, to decide future of producers' supply controls.
Last week, New York spot May futures for quality arabica beans trade at $2.80 per pound, the highest since June 1977.
The ICO said the developments in the coffee market in the past five months had been "spectacular".
"On a calendar year basis, world supply has been consistently below demand since 1993," it said.

Stocks of green cofee in the principal importing countries, including stocks in free ports, were estimated at seven million bags at the end of 1996, about half of the stocks held at the end of 1994 and nearly one-third of the stocks in December 1992.
"The fundamental elements of the market, which paradoxically had little impact on prices in 1996, seem to have influenced the market in the first months of 1997," the ICO said.

The underlying factors include supply problems in Latin America due to weather damage and industrial action in Colombia and Brazil, low stocks in the United States and the lower Brazilian crop for 1997/98.
There had also been active buying by investment funds in the New York and London futures markets and a surge in roaster demand.
But the ICO said the market is now expecting adequate supplies of arabica coffee when the new 1997/98 crop is harvested in much of Latin America during the last quarter of 1997.
"...It should be noted that with cumulative purchases by investment funds, there is always a possibility that a massive liquidation of positions could trigger large falls in prices," it said.
The current rally in bean prices had provoked increases in retail prices and the ICO said this could dampen consumption in both importing and consuming countries.

It said roasters, who have been maintaining a hand-to-mouth buying policy, were also likely to slightly readjust their stock levels to anticipate any threat to regular supplies to the market. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
